54 5 7 discussion in this study we examine the potential of a deep learning approach lstm networks in predictive analytics of lms log data in addition given the limited research comparing deep learning with conventional machine learning classifiers for predictive analytics e g jiang et al 2018 le pardos meyer thorp 2018 our study provides further evidence for the potential of deep learning to predict learning outcomes our results suggest that deep learning could be successful in predicting course performance using daily click frequencies in the lms generally the lstm networks demonstrated better prediction performance than the machine learning classifiers the performance of the eight machine learning classifiers used as baselines for our lstm approach can be discussed separately for using all features versus using selected features when all features were used as expected the auc scores on the test dataset i e semester 2 were close to their validation auc scores for most classifiers some classifiers such as na ve bayes however showed much lower auc scores on the test dataset than on the validation dataset regarding generalizability most classifiers showed poor test performance on the test dataset from the external course i e semester 1 in terms of auc scores but the performance of nn svm knn and rf were relatively better than the others when the selected top features were used all models improved in terms of validation auc scores this finding echoes the idea that using the right features may be more important than using more features since feature selection is of great importance for machine learning hall smith 1998 from the perspective of bias variance trade offs using more features may reduce the bias in training but also increases the variance in other words more features lead to better model fit to the training data represented by lower training errors however when unseen data are used for testing models often do not perform well because they are built on the features important for training but not for testing another key finding is that the most influential features for machine learning are all frequency related suggesting that time related features may not be very useful for prediction unlike in class learning activities we cannot directly observe how much time students actually spend in the lms students might head off in search of coffee leaving the system open other researchers have pointed out that time related lms features should be treated with caution e g casey azcona 2017 all features related to online sessions were also found to be of limited use in this study similarly we cannot directly observe what students actually do in each online session therefore an online session might not be a real collection of consecutive events in the lms the importance of click frequency for prediction has been observed in other studies as well for example in amrieh hamtini and aljarah s 2016 study three of the top four indicators were frequency related lms features with number of course resources visited ranked as the most important this finding also supports using daily click frequencies rather than daily time spent on the lms for time series modelling regarding the eight machine learning classifiers predictive models based on aggregated features might be of limited predictive capacity for different types of courses given the results from the biology course the testing auc scores for most machine learning classifiers were also not satisfactory particularly test performance did not differ much between the two datasets indicating that the aggregated features extracted from log files for the biology course were not good indicators of course performance furthermore the best performing classifiers were different in the two courses suggesting that predictive models should be customized for different types of courses in general the lstm networks used in the education course showed slightly higher test auc scores than the bestperforming machine learning classifiers i e svm and knn specifically the first 28 days network demonstrated a similar test performance compared with the best performing machine learning classifier the advantages of lstm networks were much more compelling for the biology course specifically the test auc scores for each were much higher than all the machine learning classifiers irrespective of test datasets notably the first 28 days data showed an auc rate around 75 on the test issn 1929 7750 online the journal of learning analytics works under a creative commons license attribution noncommercial noderivs 3 0 unported cc by nc nd 3 0 12 dataset from the same semester as the training dataset these results are promising given that in contrast to machine learning classifiers using multiple aggregated lms features lstm networks modelled a relatively simpler feature daily click frequencies which required much less feature engineering generally models using data over a longer period had better predictive performance than the first 28 days model but the test performance did not consistently increase as number of weeks increased often overlooked in previous studies we examined the generalizability evaluation of predictive models our approach was evaluated by both the test performance on a dataset from a different semester and the comparison between the two types of courses on average in contrast with the chance level of auc i e 0 5 our test auc scores were more than 20 above for both the education and biology courses however most lstm networks showed an absolute auc score above 60 for the different semester which could be considered as moderate generalizability since the use of lstm networks might be restricted by sample size when training on a small dataset a discrepancy in model performance is expected between training and testing in terms of comparing training and test performance our approach performed well for both courses with a slightly higher test performance for the biology course further validating the generalizability of our approach compared with the majority of machine learning classifiers our approach demonstrates stronger generalizability in terms of higher test auc scores for the different semesters and courses when all lms log features were used most classifiers showed a validation or test auc score below 60 consistent with previous studies e g romero et al 2013 a possible explanation is that the machine learning classifiers used multiple lms log features for prediction which introduced more variance into the model while our approach only used daily click frequencies in the lms a finding of great practical importance one major goal of the institutional application of predictive analytics is to build a flexible model that performs well for a wide range of courses this can be challenging since different courses have distinct structures teaching and learning activities and requirements deriving a set of common aggregated features which in turn limits the generalizability of conventional machine learning classifiers can be difficult however using student time series data might provide a solution as shown by our findings some previous studies demonstrated the potential of learners time series data in a variety of contexts the 2018 special issue of the journal of learning analytics on temporal analyses of learning data featured the results of several studies along these lines 1 learners temporal sequences of group talk in solving an algebra problem were analyzed with regression analyses to predict their group learning outcomes chiu 2018 2 student discourse transcripts were analyzed over time with a combination of socio semantic network analysis and dialogical discourse analysis to characterize and interpret their group discourse and collaboration practises oshima oshima fujita 2018 3 two novel measures were proposed to identify learners timing behaviours in a self paced online course and examine the time effects on learners post course self efficacy riel lawless brown 2018 4 a generalizable multi step approach was developed to analyze multimodal data to interpret learning trajectories in intelligent tutoring systems liu stamper davenport 2018 5 a sequence data model was proposed to analyze student learning records and lms activities for both a withinsemester prediction of final course grades and a between semester prediction of program completion mahzoon maher eltayeby dou grace 2018 despite these promising uses of time series data differences in data types analytical approaches and application contexts mean that generalizable intervention pathways for learners are unlikely to be developed temporal analyses of learning data applicable in a wide range of contexts however are still worth further exploration the simplicity of our approach would be beneficial for building predictive models for educational institutions in practice typically feature engineering is a burdensome and challenging task in conventional machine learning applications the features used in previous models can help to build new learning analytics models berland baker blikstein 2014 however extracted features that work well in one scenario might be ineffective in another for a course in education requiring extensive online readings for example the frequency of visits to class reading materials might be very indicative of final course performance while the same feature might be useless for predicting performance in a computer science course that emphasizes programming skills with conventional machine learning approaches model designers and developers must collaborate with course instructors to identify unique lms features tailored to each course which is unlikely feasible in practice in this sense given the importance of generalizability and simplicity it is desirable to use simple generalizable features in learning analytics applications our results suggest that daily click frequency demonstrates better predictive performance than the combination of other aggregated features and works well for two very different types of courses indicating good potential in practice although our approach is simpler and more generalizable there are still many technical considerations in designing an lstm issn 1929 7750 online the journal of learning analytics works under a creative commons license attribution noncommercial noderivs 3 0 unported cc by nc nd 3 0 13 framework for building a predictive analytics model for example model developers still need to obtain adequate data for training tuning hyperparameters and deciding the optimal time to send warnings to students compared to a set of aggregated features daily lms usage is relatively simple for instructors to understand and use course instructors can simply monitor student usage to flag at risk students review their other course activities and assignment performance and send them timely warnings through the lms this is especially beneficial for large classes e g first year introductory courses because instructors are less able to pay close attention to every student while frequent in process evaluations of student performance would be costly in addition the model built in one school year can be refined and used repeatedly in future school years which reduces the development cost in general our approach is not meant to replace other evaluation and intervention systems in higher education rather it serves as an effective screening system for flagging at risk students regardless of course type which improves efficiency and saves the cost of in process course evaluations in terms of limitations our sample sizes were quite small for predictive modelling which possibly undermines the power of the deep learning approach future studies analyzing data from courses with more students are encouraged to validate our findings another concern relates to the class imbalance for which we used the smote oversampling approach to compensate despite this oversampling still introduced bias in training given that many synthetic samples were generated in addition most machine learning models require that the training and test data come from the same feature and target distributions in our analysis the test datasets were largely imbalanced as such the difference in target class distribution between training and test data also undermined the model generalizability future studies are needed to examine how to better chapter 2 literature review 2 1 learning analytics in higher education since the early 2010s learning analytics has emerged as an established research field despite this development prediction focused learning analytics research has given less attention to the human ethical and pedagogical issues involved in institutional use siemens and long 2011 offer the field s most widely cited definition of la as the measurement collection analysis and reporting of data about learners and their contexts yet this definition does not address the question of who benefits from that analysis or how insights should be communicated to different institutional actors verbert et al 2013 argue that dashboards should treat practitioners as active users rather than passive recipients of algorithmic outputs this view supports the role aware approach adopted in this study the growth of lms platforms in higher education has produced an abundance of clickstream logs assessment histories forum activity and demographic records creating the data needed for predictive analytics but not necessarily for their effective institutional use kuzilek et al 2017 jin et al 2024 conducted a prisma compliant systematic review of 17 oulad based studies classifying machine learning approaches by predictive target academic performance at risk status and engagement level their findings confirm that ensemble methods particularly gradient boosting variants and random forests consistently outperform simpler classifiers however jin et al 2024 note that the overwhelming focus on model accuracy leaves the practitioner facing dimension of these systems largely unaddressed leitner et al 2019 review the challenges of la implementation in higher education institutions and identify a persistent disconnect between the technical sophistication of predictive models and their uptake in institutional decision making attributing this gap in part to the absence of role appropriate explanation interfaces together these studies show that predictive modelling has advanced considerably while less attention has been given to communicating predictions according to the different information needs of institutional stakeholders this study addresses that gap by proposing a role aware explainable learning analytics framework for higher education other studies have examined the purpose of learning analytics and the groups it is intended to support ferguson 2012 traces the field s emergence from earlier traditions in educational data mining and academic analytics arguing that its distinctiveness lies not in the data or algorithms it employs but in its explicit orientation towards improving learning ga evi et al 2015 similarly argue that predictive tools have developed faster than the pedagogical foundations needed to guide their use and that models which optimize for statistical accuracy without a defensible theory of learning risk producing insights that institutions cannot meaningfully act upon this study takes this critique seriously by anchoring its dashboard design not in raw predictive performance but in the decision needs of specific institutional actors the reference model proposed by chatti et al 2012 provides a useful conceptual framework for situating this study within the wider field their four dimensional taxonomy considers the data and environments analysed the stakeholders involved the objectives pursued and the methods used it therefore treats stakeholder differences as a central design concern viberg et al 2018 in a systematic review of 252 higher education learning analytics studies report that only a small fraction of published work provides evidence of measurable improvement in learning outcomes and that even fewer studies engage with the differentiated information needs of non student stakeholders this finding supports the problem addressed in this study the gap between analytical capability and institutional adoption is now well documented tsai and ga evi 2017 synthesise policy level evidence from european and australasian universities and identify a persistent shortage of practitioner facing decision support as a primary barrier to sustained adoption complementary evidence comes from larrabee s nderlund et al 2019 whose systematic review of learning analytics interventions concludes that the empirical case for improved learner outcomes remains modest largely because the interventions triggered by analytical insights are inconsistently designed and delivered together with leitner et al 2019 these studies suggest that effective learning analytics depends not only on model sophistication but also on whether institutional users can understand and act on the resulting insights this is the central premise of the study 2 2 student at risk prediction models research on predicting student at risk status has attracted sustained attention with investigations spanning logistic regression decision trees ensemble methods and deep learning architectures wang 2025 reports that a hybrid ensemble combining decision trees random forests support vector machines and artificial neural networks achieves 96 9 accuracy on oulad and 98 8 on the uci student performance dataset while rebelo marcolino et al 2025 demonstrate that catboost with nsga ii multi objective optimisation attains comparably high dropout prediction performance on moodle log data these results are consistent with jin et al 2024 who found that ensemble gradient boosting models are common in recent oulad research guevara reyes et al 2025 extend this comparison by examining interpretability trade offs across model families finding that more complex ensembles gain accuracy at the cost of intrinsic interpretability a trade off that motivates the post hoc xai integration in this study a systematic review of 33 machine learning studies by albreiki et al 2021 finds that predictive accuracy has improved substantially across the literature but that this technical progress has not been accompanied by improvements in how predictions are communicated the overwhelming majority of reviewed systems generate risk outcomes without offering educators any interpretive account of why a particular student was flagged ahmed et al 2025 further demonstrate that ensemble models with integrated shap and lime explanations are both technically feasible and accurate when applied to multi institutional academic performance datasets yet their deployment in live institutional dashboards remains rare together these reviews show a gap between the ability to predict at risk students and the ability to communicate those predictions to practitioners the growing focus on prediction within learning analytics has deep theoretical roots that the technical literature does not always make explicit tinto 1975 proposed an influential model of student departure in which academic and social integration jointly determine persistence and subsequent empirical work has operationalised his constructs through the behavioural traces captured by modern lms platforms aljohani et al 2019 show the relationship by demonstrating that clickstream indicators of engagement submission timeliness and forum participation align closely with tinto s academic integration dimension and yield reliable early warnings on the oulad dataset this theoretical background helps identify which behavioural features have pedagogical meaning and should therefore be included in the explanation views previous studies have examined several types of algorithms for at risk prediction and report some consistent findings hussain et al 2018 applied logistic regression support vector machines and neural networks to lms engagement records and reported that engagement based features consistently outperformed static demographic features across all model families adnan et al 2021 extended this line of enquiry by evaluating multiple classifiers at different points within a course and demonstrated that useful predictions can be generated after as little as 20 of the course has elapsed an important finding for institutional intervention windows f chen and cui 2020 argue that time series representations of student behaviour further improve early prediction particularly when the model can capture patterns of disengagement that unfold gradually across weeks rather than surfacing in a single indicator researchers have also investigated deep learning approaches though results are mixed relative to their computational cost waheed et al 2020 trained deep artificial neural networks on oulad and reported strong classification performance but noted that the marginal accuracy gains over well tuned ensembles were modest and did not justify the additional opacity deeper architectures introduce hassan et al 2019 reached a similar conclusion for withdrawal prediction showing that recurrent architectures capture temporal engagement patterns effectively but produce outputs that are difficult to interpret without dedicated post hoc explanation techniques these findings suggest that predictive accuracy alone is not sufficient when selecting models for institutional use interpretability and the ability to provide explanations should also be considered a further strand of the literature examines the fairness and generalizability of at risk models a concern that is directly relevant to any system that will influence intervention decisions baker and hawn 2022 provide a comprehensive review of algorithmic bias in education and document systematic disparities in model performance across demographic subgroups particularly where training data underrepresents specific student populations yu et al 2020 show using large scale institutional data that predictive models can produce systematically different error rates across gender ethnic and first generation student groups even when overall accuracy is high these studies suggest that aggregate accuracy results on oulad should be interpreted with caution an operational dashboard should also provide enough detail for practitioners to identify and question differences in model performance across groups the role aware explanation design pursued in this study is one mechanism that makes this possible several methodological refinements recur in this literature and are relevant to the design choices made later in this thesis class imbalance is commonly addressed using the synthetic minority oversampling technique smote originally introduced by chawla et al 2002 and the fifteen year retrospective analysis of fern ndez et al 2018 confirms that smote and its principled variants remain competitive with more recent resampling methods on tabular data naive oversampling can amplify noise near class boundaries for this reason researchers have proposed borderline and adaptive variants of smote prati et al 2015 describe a protocol for comparing these approaches santos et al 2018 further recommend resampling only on the training partition of each cross validation fold so oversampling before splitting does not produce optimistic bias class weighted loss functions are a common alternative since they preserve the marginal distribution of the training data hyperparameter optimisation and validation design are a second recurring concern bergstra et al 2011 provide empirical evidence that sequential model based optimisation such as bayesian optimisation with the tree structured parzen estimator outperforms grid and random search in high dimensional configuration spaces at equivalent computational budgets many oulad studies report results from stratified random splits and jin et al 2024 note that evaluation protocols vary considerably across this literature krstajic et al 2014 criticise protocols in which observations from the same higher level unit appear in both training and validation folds since this form of leakage produces optimistic estimates chicco and jurman 2020 recommend the matthews correlation coefficient as a more informative summary than accuracy or f1 alone under class imbalance and area under the precision recall curve and balanced accuracy are commonly reported as secondary metrics for the same reason probability calibration is a third consideration for systems that display risk probabilities rather than binary decisions since miscalibrated probabilities may lead practitioners to overreact to weak signals niculescu mizil and caruana 2005 compare isotonic regression and platt scaling for this purpose and guo et al 2017 quantify calibration error using reliability diagrams and expected calibration error kim et al 2024 note that trust in ai generated outputs depends not only on accuracy but also on the perceived reliability of the confidence values shown to users finally feature design matters for early prediction adnan et al 2021 provide evidence that trend based features which capture period over period change in engagement and performance improve early warning even when absolute values are stable these refinements class imbalance handling hyperparameter optimisation calibration and trajectory features were considered when planning the study s methodology chapter 3 section 3 4 explains which were used in the final evaluation and records the remainder as planned but not implemented extensions 2 3 explainable artificial intelligence a comparative analysis explainable ai has become increasingly important as high accuracy models are adopted in education the educational setting also presents particular challenges because model outputs may influence decisions about students barredo arrieta et al 2020 reviewed more than 400 papers and distinguished between interpretable models and explanation techniques they argue that the choice between these approaches depends on the deployment context and the expertise of the intended user a distinction that earlier xai surveys by gunning and aha 2019 did not address in depth ali et al 2023 extend this analysis by documenting that user type specific explanation tailoring remains an open problem across the xai literature with most systems defaulting to generic technically framed outputs that presuppose a level of ml expertise that practitioners in education typically do not possess within the educational domain shap and lime dominate current applications but their comparative strengths and limitations are contested nnadi et al 2024 evaluated shap lime anchors accumulated local effects ale and counterfactual explanations on a student adaptability dataset and found shap most consistent for feature attribution stability across model types by contrast salih et al 2025 provides a rigorous critique of both techniques noting that shap s computational overhead limits real time deployment and that lime s local approximation boundary is sensitive to sampling parameters in ways that affect reproducibility gunasekara and saarela 2025 who apply shap and lime to models trained on the oulad dataset help explain these differences prior studies have reported complementary strengths with shap commonly used for global attribution and lime for local approximations islam et al 2025 further show that combining shap shapash eli5 and lime with xgboost enables fine grained performance explanations suitable for institutional reporting though their work stops short of evaluating how non technical stakeholders receive and interpret these explanations however these studies give limited attention to how explanations should be presented to practitioners with different roles levels of expertise and decision making responsibilities afzaal et al 2021 present one of the earliest examples of an xai dashboard delivering shap based explanations within an lms directed at students rather than institutional staff while their work demonstrates the technical feasibility of embedding xai in an lms context it does not address the instructor advisor or administrator perspectives that are central to institutional at risk intervention this study focuses on the gap between the explanations produced by xai methods and the different information needs of stakeholder roles previous research on the theoretical foundations of explainable ai complements the empirical evaluations discussed above miller 2019 drawing on decades of research in cognitive and social psychology argues that explanations are inherently social contrastive and selective and that xai systems which ignore these properties tend to produce technically accurate but psychologically unsatisfying accounts of model behaviour lipton 2018 offers a parallel critique of the interpretability literature showing that the term is used inconsistently and that different notions of interpretability including simulatability decomposability and post hoc transparency imply different design choices these ideas are relevant to this study because a role aware dashboard must consider both which explanations to display and what type of interpretability each stakeholder needs a related literature has examined the limits of post hoc explanation techniques themselves adadi and berrada 2018 survey a broad taxonomy of xai methods and note that the field lacks agreed evaluation protocols making many claims about explanation quality hard to verify guidotti et al 2019 provide a complementary survey of black box explanation methods and note that fidelity the degree to which an explanation faithfully reflects the underlying model is often traded against comprehensibility in ways that are rarely reported rudin 2019 advances the strongest version of this critique by arguing that high stakes decisions should be supported by intrinsically interpretable models rather than by post hoc explanations of opaque ones although the study adopts a post hoc approach for consistency with prior oulad literature these critiques motivated the fidelity and stability checks specified for the explanation pipeline in chapter 3 section 3 5 which were proposed as safeguards but not completed in the final evaluation and they suggest caution when relying on shap or lime outputs in isolation within the educational domain khosravi et al 2022 map the state of explainable ai in education and identify six recurring stakeholder groups including learners teachers and administrators whose explanation needs differ structurally their analysis reinforces this study s central design proposition by showing that a single undifferentiated explanation view is unlikely to serve any of these groups well conati et al 2021 provide empirical support for a personalised approach through a case study within an intelligent tutoring system demonstrating that learners with different levels of prior knowledge derive substantially different value from the same underlying explanations these findings provide empirical support for designing explanations according to the needs of different users counterfactual explanations have also emerged as an increasingly important complement to feature attribution methods such as shap and lime wachter et al 2018 argue that counterfactuals answer what would have to change for a prediction to differ which is precisely what a practitioner facing an intervention decision needs to know susnjak et al 2022 integrate counterfactual reasoning into a learner facing dashboard that is deployed for trials at a higher education institution but their design addresses a single stakeholder group the literature therefore shows that counterfactual explanations are technically useful in education but their presentation for different stakeholder roles remains underexplored 2 4 dashboards in learning analytics learning analytics dashboards lads serve as the primary interface through which analytical insights reach institutional stakeholders yet the evaluation literature reveals an ongoing design limitation susnjak et al 2022 note that most existing lads confine themselves to descriptive reporting of past behaviour and they respond to this limitation by proposing a learner facing dashboard described by its authors as the first of its kind in the breadth of analytics it integrates that combines descriptive predictive and prescriptive analytics with counterfactual explanations within a single interface however this dashboard is designed for a single user group learners and does not differentiate between the varied information needs of instructors advisors and administrators this single role limitation is shared by chavan and mitra 2022 who apply iterative prototyping to an instructor facing video analytics dashboard and demonstrate improved usability but whose design does not generalise across multiple institutional stakeholder groups kaliisa and dolonen 2023 evaluate a teacher facing la dashboard through ten semi structured interviews and find that instructors prioritise summary level alerts over granular statistical breakdowns a finding that has direct implications for how the instructor interface of the present study should be designed kaliisa et al 2023 contribute a four dimensional design checklist covering purpose stakeholder involvement design and evaluation that guided this study s dashboard development methodology in a recent systematic review of ai powered learning analytics dashboards cabral et al 2025 identify limited xai integration as one of the most persistent research gaps in the field noting that xai components are absent from most of the reviewed dashboards kaliisa et al 2023 further report that although teachers are involved in designing teacher facing dashboards this involvement is mainly at the exploratory or problem definition stage with little input beyond it which risks producing designs that do not fully reflect the needs of the practitioners they are intended to serve the studies reviewed above form part of a longer effort to understand and organise the design of learning analytics dashboards schwendimann et al 2017 in a systematic review of 55 dashboards propose a taxonomy that distinguishes dashboards by their data sources intended users indicators and visualisation styles and note that only a small proportion of reviewed systems were grounded in explicit theories of learning or decision making bodily and verbert 2017 offer a complementary review focused on student facing dashboards and educational recommender systems and observe that the field has developed rich technical methods for surfacing behavioural indicators while making comparatively little progress on how intended users should interpret those indicators together with the more recent review by cabral et al 2025 these earlier reviews show that explaining analytical outputs has remained a limitation in dashboard research empirical studies of dashboard effectiveness have reported similar limitations matcha et al 2020 synthesise findings from 21 empirical studies of learning analytics dashboards through a self regulated learning lens and report that most systems are neither theoretically grounded nor evaluated against learning outcomes with most studies limited to usability measurement or short term satisfaction surveys sedrakyan et al 2020 argue that this limited evaluation is partly related to treating dashboards as reporting tools rather than as part of a wider feedback process and they call for designs that explicitly model how analytical outputs enter the practitioner s decision making process the study responds by embedding the dashboard within a commonkads communication model that treats each stakeholder role as a distinct decision making agent with its own knowledge requirements 2 5 role aware system design beyond the general dashboard design literature a smaller but growing body of work explicitly addresses the role aware presentation of analytical insights the commonkads methodology first consolidated by schreiber et al 2000 and developed further by studer et al 1998 provides one of the clearest theoretical foundations for this approach by treating agents their tasks and the knowledge they require as distinct modelling artefacts applied to learning analytics this perspective suggests that each interface should be designed around the tasks and knowledge of its intended role rather than using the same template for all users this modelling stance is adopted throughout this study human centred xai research supports this principle from another perspective liao and varshney 2022 and ehsan et al 2021 argue that an explanation s effectiveness depends on the fit between the explanation content the recipient s expertise and the decision they are trying to make and that generic explanations tend to satisfy no one particularly well kouki et al 2020 provide empirical evidence for this claim in the context of hybrid recommender systems showing that personalised explanations that adapt to user characteristics outperform undifferentiated explanations on measures of perceived usefulness and satisfaction although these studies are not situated within education their findings can be applied to the differentiated instructor advisor and administrator interfaces proposed in this study empirical work within learning analytics has begun to converge on similar conclusions kaliisa et al 2023 argue that dashboard design must move beyond a single archetypal user and explicitly engage with the plurality of stakeholders whose decisions the system will inform guti rrez et al 2020 in an evaluation of the lada advising dashboard demonstrate that even a single stakeholder role encompasses substantial variation in information needs with senior advisors preferring cohort level views and less experienced advisors relying more heavily on individual case detail kaliisa et al 2023 bring these issues together in a checklist covering stakeholder involvement design and evaluation this checklist informs both the design and evaluation of the present study the studies reviewed show a consistent pattern the technical components required to generate predictions and shap or lime explanations are now relatively mature and widely available however methodological approaches for translating shared computational outputs into role appropriate interface content remain less developed this study addresses this gap by combining the commonkads agent and communication models with the kaliisa et al 2023 design checklist this provides a structured way to move from stakeholder analysis to role specific interface content 2 6 research gap the literature reviewed in this chapter identifies a gap at the intersection of student at risk prediction explainable ai and role aware learning analytics dashboard design several specific interrelated dimensions of this gap warrant more attention and study first although ensemble models have achieved high accuracy on oulad and similar datasets guevara reyes et al 2025 jin et al 2024 rebelo marcolino et al 2025 wang 2025 the reviewed studies give limited attention to how their predictions are communicated to practitioners evaluation in this area remains largely technical with accuracy f1 score and auc commonly reported while the interpretability of model outputs receives less attention second the xai literature including ali et al 2023 barredo arrieta et al 2020 gunasekara saarela 2025 islam et al 2025 nnadi et al 2024 salih et al 2025 demonstrates that post hoc explanation methods can be used in educational settings but gives less attention to how explanations should differ between institutional stakeholder roles the only role specific xai dashboard identified in the literature reviewed for this study afzaal et al 2021 targets students not the instructors advisors and administrators responsible for institutional intervention decisions thirdly the dashboard design literature cabral et al 2025 chavan mitra 2022 kaliisa dolonen 2023 susnjak et al 2022 consistently demonstrates that existing lads serve a single stakeholder type or provide undifferentiated role agnostic outputs the literature reviewed in this study did not identify a study that has designed implemented and empirically evaluated a dashboard that serves three distinct lms stakeholder roles instructors advisors and administrators from a single shared prediction system with role specific xai explanations the knowledge engineering aspect of xai dashboard development has also received limited attention in particular existing studies have given little attention to how shap and lime outputs can be represented as knowledge and delivered differently to different stakeholder roles this can be viewed as a knowledge engineering problem applying a structured knowledge engineering methodology such as commonkads schreiber et al 2000 to this context provides the methodological contribution of the study finally the evaluation frameworks used in existing xai studies al ansari et al 2024 kim et al 2024 are largely generic and give limited attention to differences in trust understanding and decision quality across lms stakeholder groups this study addresses these issues through a technically evaluated artefact and a proposed framework for future expert validation the dashboard is designed around different stakeholder roles and the commonkads knowledge engineering framework taken together these five gaps point to a broader problem technical methodological and evaluation work has often developed separately and the few studies that combine them generally focus on a single stakeholder group this study therefore designs the predictive model explanation layer role aware interface and evaluation framework against a common knowledge engineering specification based on these findings the study extends previous work by bringing these areas together to address a gap that earlier research has given limited attention to 2 7 chapter summary this chapter reviewed research on learning analytics student at risk prediction explainable ai and learning analytics dashboard design the review showed how these areas contribute to the problem addressed by this study while also identifying their limitations the conceptual and empirical reviews confirm that ensemble predictive models can identify at risk students with high accuracy on benchmark datasets such as oulad that post hoc explanation techniques including shap and lime are technically mature and that learning analytics dashboards are widely deployed the review also showed that high predictive accuracy does not necessarily translate into institutional impact explanation methods are rarely tailored to different users and many dashboards continue to focus on a single type of user despite differences in stakeholder information needs the research gap identified above follows from these findings the remainder of the thesis uses the commonkads knowledge engineering framework together with the kaliisa et al 2023 design checklist and the human centred evaluation framework of kim et al 2024 to address these limitations the chapter therefore provides both the theoretical grounding and the empirical justification for the role aware explainable ai dashboard developed and technically evaluated in the chapters that follow
abstract this study investigates current approaches to learning analytics la dashboarding while highlighting challenges faced by education providers in their operationalization we analyze recent dashboards for their ability to provide actionable insights which promote informed responses by learners in making adjustments to their learning habits our study finds that most la dashboards merely employ surface level descriptive analytics while only few go beyond and use predictive analytics in response to the identified gaps in recently published dashboards we propose a state of the art dashboard that not only leverages descriptive analytics components but also integrates machine learning in a way that enables both predictive and prescriptive analytics we demonstrate how emerging analytics tools can be used in order to enable learners to adequately interpret the predictive model behavior and more specifically to understand how a predictive model arrives at a given prediction we highlight how these capabilities build trust and satisfy emerging regulatory requirements surrounding predictive analytics additionally we show how data driven prescriptive analytics can be deployed within dashboards in order to provide concrete advice to the learners and thereby increase the likelihood of triggering behavioral changes our proposed dashboard is the first of its kind in terms of breadth of analytics that it integrates and is currently deployed for trials at a higher education institution
