chapter 2 literature review 2 1 learning analytics in higher education since the early 2010s learning analytics has emerged as an established research field despite this development prediction focused learning analytics research has given less attention to the human ethical and pedagogical issues involved in institutional use siemens and long 2011 offer the field s most widely cited definition of la as the measurement collection analysis and reporting of data about learners and their contexts yet this definition does not address the question of who benefits from that analysis or how insights should be communicated to different institutional actors verbert et al 2013 argue that dashboards should treat practitioners as active users rather than passive recipients of algorithmic outputs this view supports the role aware approach adopted in this study the growth of lms platforms in higher education has produced an abundance of clickstream logs assessment histories forum activity and demographic records creating the data needed for predictive analytics but not necessarily for their effective institutional use kuzilek et al 2017 jin et al 2024 conducted a prisma compliant systematic review of 17 oulad based studies classifying machine learning approaches by predictive target academic performance at risk status and engagement level their findings confirm that ensemble methods particularly gradient boosting variants and random forests consistently outperform simpler classifiers however jin et al 2024 note that the overwhelming focus on model accuracy leaves the practitioner facing dimension of these systems largely unaddressed leitner et al 2019 review the challenges of la implementation in higher education institutions and identify a persistent disconnect between the technical sophistication of predictive models and their uptake in institutional decision making attributing this gap in part to the absence of role appropriate explanation interfaces together these studies show that predictive modelling has advanced considerably while less attention has been given to communicating predictions according to the different information needs of institutional stakeholders this study addresses that gap by proposing a role aware explainable learning analytics framework for higher education other studies have examined the purpose of learning analytics and the groups it is intended to support ferguson 2012 traces the field s emergence from earlier traditions in educational data mining and academic analytics arguing that its distinctiveness lies not in the data or algorithms it employs but in its explicit orientation towards improving learning ga evi et al 2015 similarly argue that predictive tools have developed faster than the pedagogical foundations needed to guide their use and that models which optimize for statistical accuracy without a defensible theory of learning risk producing insights that institutions cannot meaningfully act upon this study takes this critique seriously by anchoring its dashboard design not in raw predictive performance but in the decision needs of specific institutional actors the reference model proposed by chatti et al 2012 provides a useful conceptual framework for situating this study within the wider field their four dimensional taxonomy considers the data and environments analysed the stakeholders involved the objectives pursued and the methods used it therefore treats stakeholder differences as a central design concern viberg et al 2018 in a systematic review of 252 higher education learning analytics studies report that only a small fraction of published work provides evidence of measurable improvement in learning outcomes and that even fewer studies engage with the differentiated information needs of non student stakeholders this finding supports the problem addressed in this study the gap between analytical capability and institutional adoption is now well documented tsai and ga evi 2017 synthesise policy level evidence from european and australasian universities and identify a persistent shortage of practitioner facing decision support as a primary barrier to sustained adoption complementary evidence comes from larrabee s nderlund et al 2019 whose systematic review of learning analytics interventions concludes that the empirical case for improved learner outcomes remains modest largely because the interventions triggered by analytical insights are inconsistently designed and delivered together with leitner et al 2019 these studies suggest that effective learning analytics depends not only on model sophistication but also on whether institutional users can understand and act on the resulting insights this is the central premise of the study 2 2 student at risk prediction models research on predicting student at risk status has attracted sustained attention with investigations spanning logistic regression decision trees ensemble methods and deep learning architectures wang 2025 reports that a hybrid ensemble combining decision trees random forests support vector machines and artificial neural networks achieves 96 9 accuracy on oulad and 98 8 on the uci student performance dataset while rebelo marcolino et al 2025 demonstrate that catboost with nsga ii multi objective optimisation attains comparably high dropout prediction performance on moodle log data these results are consistent with jin et al 2024 who found that ensemble gradient boosting models are common in recent oulad research guevara reyes et al 2025 extend this comparison by examining interpretability trade offs across model families finding that more complex ensembles gain accuracy at the cost of intrinsic interpretability a trade off that motivates the post hoc xai integration in this study a systematic review of 33 machine learning studies by albreiki et al 2021 finds that predictive accuracy has improved substantially across the literature but that this technical progress has not been accompanied by improvements in how predictions are communicated the overwhelming majority of reviewed systems generate risk outcomes without offering educators any interpretive account of why a particular student was flagged ahmed et al 2025 further demonstrate that ensemble models with integrated shap and lime explanations are both technically feasible and accurate when applied to multi institutional academic performance datasets yet their deployment in live institutional dashboards remains rare together these reviews show a gap between the ability to predict at risk students and the ability to communicate those predictions to practitioners the growing focus on prediction within learning analytics has deep theoretical roots that the technical literature does not always make explicit tinto 1975 proposed an influential model of student departure in which academic and social integration jointly determine persistence and subsequent empirical work has operationalised his constructs through the behavioural traces captured by modern lms platforms aljohani et al 2019 show the relationship by demonstrating that clickstream indicators of engagement submission timeliness and forum participation align closely with tinto s academic integration dimension and yield reliable early warnings on the oulad dataset this theoretical background helps identify which behavioural features have pedagogical meaning and should therefore be included in the explanation views previous studies have examined several types of algorithms for at risk prediction and report some consistent findings hussain et al 2018 applied logistic regression support vector machines and neural networks to lms engagement records and reported that engagement based features consistently outperformed static demographic features across all model families adnan et al 2021 extended this line of enquiry by evaluating multiple classifiers at different points within a course and demonstrated that useful predictions can be generated after as little as 20 of the course has elapsed an important finding for institutional intervention windows f chen and cui 2020 argue that time series representations of student behaviour further improve early prediction particularly when the model can capture patterns of disengagement that unfold gradually across weeks rather than surfacing in a single indicator researchers have also investigated deep learning approaches though results are mixed relative to their computational cost waheed et al 2020 trained deep artificial neural networks on oulad and reported strong classification performance but noted that the marginal accuracy gains over well tuned ensembles were modest and did not justify the additional opacity deeper architectures introduce hassan et al 2019 reached a similar conclusion for withdrawal prediction showing that recurrent architectures capture temporal engagement patterns effectively but produce outputs that are difficult to interpret without dedicated post hoc explanation techniques these findings suggest that predictive accuracy alone is not sufficient when selecting models for institutional use interpretability and the ability to provide explanations should also be considered a further strand of the literature examines the fairness and generalizability of at risk models a concern that is directly relevant to any system that will influence intervention decisions baker and hawn 2022 provide a comprehensive review of algorithmic bias in education and document systematic disparities in model performance across demographic subgroups particularly where training data underrepresents specific student populations yu et al 2020 show using large scale institutional data that predictive models can produce systematically different error rates across gender ethnic and first generation student groups even when overall accuracy is high these studies suggest that aggregate accuracy results on oulad should be interpreted with caution an operational dashboard should also provide enough detail for practitioners to identify and question differences in model performance across groups the role aware explanation design pursued in this study is one mechanism that makes this possible several methodological refinements recur in this literature and are relevant to the design choices made later in this thesis class imbalance is commonly addressed using the synthetic minority oversampling technique smote originally introduced by chawla et al 2002 and the fifteen year retrospective analysis of fern ndez et al 2018 confirms that smote and its principled variants remain competitive with more recent resampling methods on tabular data naive oversampling can amplify noise near class boundaries for this reason researchers have proposed borderline and adaptive variants of smote prati et al 2015 describe a protocol for comparing these approaches santos et al 2018 further recommend resampling only on the training partition of each cross validation fold so oversampling before splitting does not produce optimistic bias class weighted loss functions are a common alternative since they preserve the marginal distribution of the training data hyperparameter optimisation and validation design are a second recurring concern bergstra et al 2011 provide empirical evidence that sequential model based optimisation such as bayesian optimisation with the tree structured parzen estimator outperforms grid and random search in high dimensional configuration spaces at equivalent computational budgets many oulad studies report results from stratified random splits and jin et al 2024 note that evaluation protocols vary considerably across this literature krstajic et al 2014 criticise protocols in which observations from the same higher level unit appear in both training and validation folds since this form of leakage produces optimistic estimates chicco and jurman 2020 recommend the matthews correlation coefficient as a more informative summary than accuracy or f1 alone under class imbalance and area under the precision recall curve and balanced accuracy are commonly reported as secondary metrics for the same reason probability calibration is a third consideration for systems that display risk probabilities rather than binary decisions since miscalibrated probabilities may lead practitioners to overreact to weak signals niculescu mizil and caruana 2005 compare isotonic regression and platt scaling for this purpose and guo et al 2017 quantify calibration error using reliability diagrams and expected calibration error kim et al 2024 note that trust in ai generated outputs depends not only on accuracy but also on the perceived reliability of the confidence values shown to users finally feature design matters for early prediction adnan et al 2021 provide evidence that trend based features which capture period over period change in engagement and performance improve early warning even when absolute values are stable these refinements class imbalance handling hyperparameter optimisation calibration and trajectory features were considered when planning the study s methodology chapter 3 section 3 4 explains which were used in the final evaluation and records the remainder as planned but not implemented extensions 2 3 explainable artificial intelligence a comparative analysis explainable ai has become increasingly important as high accuracy models are adopted in education the educational setting also presents particular challenges because model outputs may influence decisions about students barredo arrieta et al 2020 reviewed more than 400 papers and distinguished between interpretable models and explanation techniques they argue that the choice between these approaches depends on the deployment context and the expertise of the intended user a distinction that earlier xai surveys by gunning and aha 2019 did not address in depth ali et al 2023 extend this analysis by documenting that user type specific explanation tailoring remains an open problem across the xai literature with most systems defaulting to generic technically framed outputs that presuppose a level of ml expertise that practitioners in education typically do not possess within the educational domain shap and lime dominate current applications but their comparative strengths and limitations are contested nnadi et al 2024 evaluated shap lime anchors accumulated local effects ale and counterfactual explanations on a student adaptability dataset and found shap most consistent for feature attribution stability across model types by contrast salih et al 2025 provides a rigorous critique of both techniques noting that shap s computational overhead limits real time deployment and that lime s local approximation boundary is sensitive to sampling parameters in ways that affect reproducibility gunasekara and saarela 2025 who apply shap and lime to models trained on the oulad dataset help explain these differences prior studies have reported complementary strengths with shap commonly used for global attribution and lime for local approximations islam et al 2025 further show that combining shap shapash eli5 and lime with xgboost enables fine grained performance explanations suitable for institutional reporting though their work stops short of evaluating how non technical stakeholders receive and interpret these explanations however these studies give limited attention to how explanations should be presented to practitioners with different roles levels of expertise and decision making responsibilities afzaal et al 2021 present one of the earliest examples of an xai dashboard delivering shap based explanations within an lms directed at students rather than institutional staff while their work demonstrates the technical feasibility of embedding xai in an lms context it does not address the instructor advisor or administrator perspectives that are central to institutional at risk intervention this study focuses on the gap between the explanations produced by xai methods and the different information needs of stakeholder roles previous research on the theoretical foundations of explainable ai complements the empirical evaluations discussed above miller 2019 drawing on decades of research in cognitive and social psychology argues that explanations are inherently social contrastive and selective and that xai systems which ignore these properties tend to produce technically accurate but psychologically unsatisfying accounts of model behaviour lipton 2018 offers a parallel critique of the interpretability literature showing that the term is used inconsistently and that different notions of interpretability including simulatability decomposability and post hoc transparency imply different design choices these ideas are relevant to this study because a role aware dashboard must consider both which explanations to display and what type of interpretability each stakeholder needs a related literature has examined the limits of post hoc explanation techniques themselves adadi and berrada 2018 survey a broad taxonomy of xai methods and note that the field lacks agreed evaluation protocols making many claims about explanation quality hard to verify guidotti et al 2019 provide a complementary survey of black box explanation methods and note that fidelity the degree to which an explanation faithfully reflects the underlying model is often traded against comprehensibility in ways that are rarely reported rudin 2019 advances the strongest version of this critique by arguing that high stakes decisions should be supported by intrinsically interpretable models rather than by post hoc explanations of opaque ones although the study adopts a post hoc approach for consistency with prior oulad literature these critiques motivated the fidelity and stability checks specified for the explanation pipeline in chapter 3 section 3 5 which were proposed as safeguards but not completed in the final evaluation and they suggest caution when relying on shap or lime outputs in isolation within the educational domain khosravi et al 2022 map the state of explainable ai in education and identify six recurring stakeholder groups including learners teachers and administrators whose explanation needs differ structurally their analysis reinforces this study s central design proposition by showing that a single undifferentiated explanation view is unlikely to serve any of these groups well conati et al 2021 provide empirical support for a personalised approach through a case study within an intelligent tutoring system demonstrating that learners with different levels of prior knowledge derive substantially different value from the same underlying explanations these findings provide empirical support for designing explanations according to the needs of different users counterfactual explanations have also emerged as an increasingly important complement to feature attribution methods such as shap and lime wachter et al 2018 argue that counterfactuals answer what would have to change for a prediction to differ which is precisely what a practitioner facing an intervention decision needs to know susnjak et al 2022 integrate counterfactual reasoning into a learner facing dashboard that is deployed for trials at a higher education institution but their design addresses a single stakeholder group the literature therefore shows that counterfactual explanations are technically useful in education but their presentation for different stakeholder roles remains underexplored 2 4 dashboards in learning analytics learning analytics dashboards lads serve as the primary interface through which analytical insights reach institutional stakeholders yet the evaluation literature reveals an ongoing design limitation susnjak et al 2022 note that most existing lads confine themselves to descriptive reporting of past behaviour and they respond to this limitation by proposing a learner facing dashboard described by its authors as the first of its kind in the breadth of analytics it integrates that combines descriptive predictive and prescriptive analytics with counterfactual explanations within a single interface however this dashboard is designed for a single user group learners and does not differentiate between the varied information needs of instructors advisors and administrators this single role limitation is shared by chavan and mitra 2022 who apply iterative prototyping to an instructor facing video analytics dashboard and demonstrate improved usability but whose design does not generalise across multiple institutional stakeholder groups kaliisa and dolonen 2023 evaluate a teacher facing la dashboard through ten semi structured interviews and find that instructors prioritise summary level alerts over granular statistical breakdowns a finding that has direct implications for how the instructor interface of the present study should be designed kaliisa et al 2023 contribute a four dimensional design checklist covering purpose stakeholder involvement design and evaluation that guided this study s dashboard development methodology in a recent systematic review of ai powered learning analytics dashboards cabral et al 2025 identify limited xai integration as one of the most persistent research gaps in the field noting that xai components are absent from most of the reviewed dashboards kaliisa et al 2023 further report that although teachers are involved in designing teacher facing dashboards this involvement is mainly at the exploratory or problem definition stage with little input beyond it which risks producing designs that do not fully reflect the needs of the practitioners they are intended to serve the studies reviewed above form part of a longer effort to understand and organise the design of learning analytics dashboards schwendimann et al 2017 in a systematic review of 55 dashboards propose a taxonomy that distinguishes dashboards by their data sources intended users indicators and visualisation styles and note that only a small proportion of reviewed systems were grounded in explicit theories of learning or decision making bodily and verbert 2017 offer a complementary review focused on student facing dashboards and educational recommender systems and observe that the field has developed rich technical methods for surfacing behavioural indicators while making comparatively little progress on how intended users should interpret those indicators together with the more recent review by cabral et al 2025 these earlier reviews show that explaining analytical outputs has remained a limitation in dashboard research empirical studies of dashboard effectiveness have reported similar limitations matcha et al 2020 synthesise findings from 21 empirical studies of learning analytics dashboards through a self regulated learning lens and report that most systems are neither theoretically grounded nor evaluated against learning outcomes with most studies limited to usability measurement or short term satisfaction surveys sedrakyan et al 2020 argue that this limited evaluation is partly related to treating dashboards as reporting tools rather than as part of a wider feedback process and they call for designs that explicitly model how analytical outputs enter the practitioner s decision making process the study responds by embedding the dashboard within a commonkads communication model that treats each stakeholder role as a distinct decision making agent with its own knowledge requirements 2 5 role aware system design beyond the general dashboard design literature a smaller but growing body of work explicitly addresses the role aware presentation of analytical insights the commonkads methodology first consolidated by schreiber et al 2000 and developed further by studer et al 1998 provides one of the clearest theoretical foundations for this approach by treating agents their tasks and the knowledge they require as distinct modelling artefacts applied to learning analytics this perspective suggests that each interface should be designed around the tasks and knowledge of its intended role rather than using the same template for all users this modelling stance is adopted throughout this study human centred xai research supports this principle from another perspective liao and varshney 2022 and ehsan et al 2021 argue that an explanation s effectiveness depends on the fit between the explanation content the recipient s expertise and the decision they are trying to make and that generic explanations tend to satisfy no one particularly well kouki et al 2020 provide empirical evidence for this claim in the context of hybrid recommender systems showing that personalised explanations that adapt to user characteristics outperform undifferentiated explanations on measures of perceived usefulness and satisfaction although these studies are not situated within education their findings can be applied to the differentiated instructor advisor and administrator interfaces proposed in this study empirical work within learning analytics has begun to converge on similar conclusions kaliisa et al 2023 argue that dashboard design must move beyond a single archetypal user and explicitly engage with the plurality of stakeholders whose decisions the system will inform guti rrez et al 2020 in an evaluation of the lada advising dashboard demonstrate that even a single stakeholder role encompasses substantial variation in information needs with senior advisors preferring cohort level views and less experienced advisors relying more heavily on individual case detail kaliisa et al 2023 bring these issues together in a checklist covering stakeholder involvement design and evaluation this checklist informs both the design and evaluation of the present study the studies reviewed show a consistent pattern the technical components required to generate predictions and shap or lime explanations are now relatively mature and widely available however methodological approaches for translating shared computational outputs into role appropriate interface content remain less developed this study addresses this gap by combining the commonkads agent and communication models with the kaliisa et al 2023 design checklist this provides a structured way to move from stakeholder analysis to role specific interface content 2 6 research gap the literature reviewed in this chapter identifies a gap at the intersection of student at risk prediction explainable ai and role aware learning analytics dashboard design several specific interrelated dimensions of this gap warrant more attention and study first although ensemble models have achieved high accuracy on oulad and similar datasets guevara reyes et al 2025 jin et al 2024 rebelo marcolino et al 2025 wang 2025 the reviewed studies give limited attention to how their predictions are communicated to practitioners evaluation in this area remains largely technical with accuracy f1 score and auc commonly reported while the interpretability of model outputs receives less attention second the xai literature including ali et al 2023 barredo arrieta et al 2020 gunasekara saarela 2025 islam et al 2025 nnadi et al 2024 salih et al 2025 demonstrates that post hoc explanation methods can be used in educational settings but gives less attention to how explanations should differ between institutional stakeholder roles the only role specific xai dashboard identified in the literature reviewed for this study afzaal et al 2021 targets students not the instructors advisors and administrators responsible for institutional intervention decisions thirdly the dashboard design literature cabral et al 2025 chavan mitra 2022 kaliisa dolonen 2023 susnjak et al 2022 consistently demonstrates that existing lads serve a single stakeholder type or provide undifferentiated role agnostic outputs the literature reviewed in this study did not identify a study that has designed implemented and empirically evaluated a dashboard that serves three distinct lms stakeholder roles instructors advisors and administrators from a single shared prediction system with role specific xai explanations the knowledge engineering aspect of xai dashboard development has also received limited attention in particular existing studies have given little attention to how shap and lime outputs can be represented as knowledge and delivered differently to different stakeholder roles this can be viewed as a knowledge engineering problem applying a structured knowledge engineering methodology such as commonkads schreiber et al 2000 to this context provides the methodological contribution of the study finally the evaluation frameworks used in existing xai studies al ansari et al 2024 kim et al 2024 are largely generic and give limited attention to differences in trust understanding and decision quality across lms stakeholder groups this study addresses these issues through a technically evaluated artefact and a proposed framework for future expert validation the dashboard is designed around different stakeholder roles and the commonkads knowledge engineering framework taken together these five gaps point to a broader problem technical methodological and evaluation work has often developed separately and the few studies that combine them generally focus on a single stakeholder group this study therefore designs the predictive model explanation layer role aware interface and evaluation framework against a common knowledge engineering specification based on these findings the study extends previous work by bringing these areas together to address a gap that earlier research has given limited attention to 2 7 chapter summary this chapter reviewed research on learning analytics student at risk prediction explainable ai and learning analytics dashboard design the review showed how these areas contribute to the problem addressed by this study while also identifying their limitations the conceptual and empirical reviews confirm that ensemble predictive models can identify at risk students with high accuracy on benchmark datasets such as oulad that post hoc explanation techniques including shap and lime are technically mature and that learning analytics dashboards are widely deployed the review also showed that high predictive accuracy does not necessarily translate into institutional impact explanation methods are rarely tailored to different users and many dashboards continue to focus on a single type of user despite differences in stakeholder information needs the research gap identified above follows from these findings the remainder of the thesis uses the commonkads knowledge engineering framework together with the kaliisa et al 2023 design checklist and the human centred evaluation framework of kim et al 2024 to address these limitations the chapter therefore provides both the theoretical grounding and the empirical justification for the role aware explainable ai dashboard developed and technically evaluated in the chapters that follow
the synthetic minority oversampling technique smote preprocessing algorithm is considered de facto standard in the framework of learning from imbalanced data this is due to its simplicity in the design of the procedure as well as its robustness when applied to different type of problems since its publication in 2002 smote has proven successful in a variety of applications from several different domains smote has also inspired several approaches to counter the issue of class imbalance and has also significantly contributed to new supervised learning paradigms including multilabel classification incremental learning semi supervised learning multi instance learning among others it is standard benchmark for learning from imbalanced data it is also featured in a number of different software packages from open source to commercial in this paper marking the fifteen year anniversary of smote we reflect on the smote journey discuss the current state of affairs with smote its applications and also identify the next set of challenges to extend smote for big data problems journal of artificial intelligence research 61 2018 863 905 submitted 06 17 published 04 18 smote for learning from imbalanced data progress and challenges marking the 15 year anniversary alberto ferna ndez salvador garc a francisco herrera alberto decsai ugr es salvagl decsai ugr es herrera decsai ugr es department of computer science and artificial intelligence university of granada spain nitesh v chawla nchawla nd edu department of computer science and engineering and interdisciplinary center for network science applications university of notre dame in usa abstract the synthetic minority oversampling technique smote preprocessing algorithm is considered de facto standard in the framework of learning from imbalanced data this is due to its simplicity in the design of the procedure as well as its robustness when applied to different type of problems since its publication in 2002 smote has proven successful in a variety of applications from several different domains smote has also inspired several approaches to counter the issue of class imbalance and has also significantly contributed to new supervised learning paradigms including multilabel classification incremental learning semi supervised learning multi instance learning among others it is standard benchmark for learning from imbalanced data it is also featured in a number of different software packages from open source to commercial in this paper marking the fifteen year anniversary of smote we reflect on the smote journey discuss the current state of affairs with smote its applications and also identify the next set of challenges to extend smote for big data problems 1 introduction in the 1990s as more data and applications of machine learning and data mining started to become prevalent an important challenge emerged how to achieve desired classification accuracy when dealing with data that had significantly skewed class distributions sun et al 2009 he garcia 2009 lo pez et al 2013 branco et al 2016 cieslak et al 2012 hoens et al 2012b hoens chawla 2013 lemaitre et al 2017 khan et al 2018 authors from several disciplines observed an unexpected behavior for standard classification algorithms over datasets with uneven class distributions anand mehrotra mohan ranka 1993 bruzzone serpico 1997 kubat holte matwin 1998 in many cases the specificity or local accuracy on the majority class examples overwhelmed the one achieved on the minority ones this led to the beginning of an active area of research in machine learning now termed as learning from imbalanced data it was in the beginning of the 2000 s when the foundations of the topic were established during the first workshop on class imbalanced c 2018 ai access foundation all rights reserved ferna ndez garc a herrera chawla learning during the american association for artificial intelligence conference japkowicz holte 2000 the second milestone was set in 2003 during the icml kdd workshop on learning from imbalanced datasets leading to a special issue on the topic chawla japkowicz kolcz 2004 the significance of this area of research continues to grow largely driven by the challenging problem statements from different application areas such as face recognition software engineering social media social networks and medical diagnosis providing a novel and contemporaneous set of challenges to the machine learning and data science researchers krawczyk 2016 haixiang et al 2017 maua galinac grbac 2017 zhang et al 2017 zuo et al 2016 lichtenwalter et al 2010 krawczyk et al 2016 bach et al 2017 cao et al 2017a the overarching question that researchers have been trying to solve is how to push the boundaries of prediction on the underrepresented or minority classes while managing the trade off with with false positives the solution space has ranged from sampling approaches to new learning algorithms designed specifically for imbalanced data the sampling approaches are broadly divided into two broad categories undersampling or oversampling undersampling techniques are known to provide a compact balanced training set that also reduces the cost of the learning stage however it also leads to some derived problems first it increases the variance of the classifier and ii it produces warped posterior probabilities dal pozzolo caelen bontempi 2015 it may also might discard some useful examples for the modeling of the classifier particularly when the ratio of imbalance is high then more examples need to be removed leading to the problem of lack of data wasikowski chen 2010 this may affect the generalization ability of the classifier as a result researchers developed oversampling methods that may not lead to reduction of majority class examples and tackle the class imbalance issue by replicating the minority class examples however applying random oversampling only implies a higher weight or cost for the minority instances therefore the correct modeling of those clusters of minority data by the classification algorithm might still be hard in the case of overlapping garc a mollineda sa nchez 2008 cieslak chawla 2008 or small disjuncts jo japkowicz 2004 in 2002 chawla bowyer hall and kegelmeyer 2002 proposed a novel approach as an alternative to the standard random oversampling the idea was to overcome the overfitting rendered by simply oversampling by replication and assist the classifier to improve its generalization on the testing data instead of weighting data points the basis of this new data preprocessing technique was to create new minority instances this technique was titled synthetic minority oversampling technique now widely known as smote chawla et al 2002 the basis of the smote procedure was to carry out an interpolation among neighboring minority class instances as such it is able to increase the number of minority class instances by introducing new minority class examples in the neighborhood thereby assisting the classifiers to improve its generalization capacity smote preprocessing technique became a pioneer for the research community in imbalanced classification since its release many extensions and alternatives have been proposed to improve its performance under different scenarios due to its popularity and influence smote is considered as one of the most influential data preprocessing sampling algorithms in machine learning and data mining garc a luengo herrera 2016 some approaches 864 smote for learning from imbalanced data 15 year anniversary combine smote with data cleaning techniques batista prati monard 2004 other authors focus on the inner procedure by modifying some of its components such as the selection of the instances for new data generation han wang mao 2005 or the type of interpolation bunkhumpornpat sinapiromsaran lursinsap 2012 among others in this paper we present a summary of smote and its impact in the last 15 years celebrate its contributions to machine learning and data mining and present the next state of challenges to keep pushing the frontier on learning from imbalanced data while we don t include a discussion on the over 5 370 citations of smote as of feb 1st 2018 we specifically focus this paper on enumerating various smote extensions as well as discussing the road ahead for example we discuss the extensions of smote to other learning paradigms such as streaming data krawczyk et al 2017 brzezinski stefanowski 2017 hoens et al 2011 incremental learning ditzler polikar chawla 2010 concept drift hoens chawla 2012 hoens polikar chawla 2012a or multi label multi instance classification tasks herrera et al 2016a 2016b among others we also present an analysis about potential scenarios within imbalanced data that require a deeper dive into application of smote such as the data intrinsic characteristics lo pez et al 2013 including small disjuncts overlapping classes and so on finally we posit challenges of imbalanced classification in big data problems fernandez del rio chawla herrera 2017 our hope is that this paper provides a summative overview of smote its extensions and challenges that remain to be addressed in the community this paper is organized as follows section 2 introduces the smote algorithm then section 3 enumerates those extensions to the standard smote that have been proposed along these years section 4 presents the use of smote under different learning paradigms the challenges and topics for future work on smote based preprocessing algorithms are given in section 5 finally section 6 summarizes and concludes the paper 2 synthetic minority oversampling technique in this section we will first point out the origins of the smote algorithm setting the context under which it was designed section 2 1 then we will describe its properties in detail in order to present the working procedure of this preprocessing approach section 2 2 2 1 why to propose smote chawla reminisces the origins of smote to a classification problem that he was tackling as a graduate student in 2000 he was working on developing a classification algorithm to learn and predict about cancerous pixels the mammography data discussed in the original paper a basic decision tree classifier provided him with an accuracy of around 97 his first reaction was celebratory as he achieved over 97 accuracy on a problem that was presented as a challenge to him however that celebration was short lived he quickly realized that merely by guessing majority class he would have achieved an accuracy of 97 68 which was the majority class distribution in the original data so he actually did worse than a majority class guess classifier moreover the decision tree classifier performed poorly in the important task of predicting calcifications correctly this thus presented the challenge of how to improve the performance of the classifier on minority class instances 865 ferna ndez garc a herrera chawla an accompanying challenge was a low tolerance of false positives i e examples of the majority class identified as minority ones that is one had to achieve an appropriate trade off between the true positives and false positives and not just be overly aggressive in predicting minority class cancerous pixels to compensate for the 2 32 distribution this was because there were costs associated with errors every false negative bore the burden of misclassifying a cancer as non cancer and every false positive bore the cost of additional tests by misclassifying a non cancer as a cancer the errors clearly were not of equal types chawla tried the standard tools in the research arsenal at that time oversampling by replication and undersampling both of the approaches while improving the performance did not provide satisfactorily results on further investigation he noticed the challenge arising from overfitting the minority class instances because of oversampling this observation led to the question of how to improve the generalization capacity of the underling classifier and thus smote was created to synthetically generate new instances to provide new information to the learning algorithm to improve its predictability about the minority class instances smote provided statistically significantly superior performance on the mammography data as well as several others thus laying the foundation for learning from imbalanced datasets of course smote like other sampling approaches faces the challenge of the sampling amount which chawla and his colleagues also tried to mitigate by developing a wrapper framework akin to feature selection chawla cieslak hall joshi 2008 2 2 smote description the smote algorithm carries out an oversampling approach to rebalance the original training set instead of applying a simple replication of the minority class instances the key idea of smote is to introduce synthetic examples this new data is created by interpolation between several minority class instances that are within a defined neighborhood for this reason the procedure is said to be focused on the feature space rather than on the data space in other words the algorithm is based on the values of the features and their relationship instead of considering the data points as a whole this has also led to studying the theoretical relationship between original and synthetic instances must be analyzed in depth including the data dimensionality some properties such as variance and correlation in the data and feature space as well as the relationship between training and test examples distribution must be considered blagus lusa 2013 we will discuss these issues hereinafter in section 5 a simple example of smote is illustrated in figure 1 an xi minority class instance is selected as basis to create new synthetic data points based on a distance metric several nearest neighbors of the same class points xi1 to xi4 are chosen from the training set finally a randomized interpolation is carried out in order to obtain new instances r1 to r4 the formal procedure works as follows first the total amount of oversampling n an integer value is set up which can either be set up to obtain an approximate 1 1 class distribution or discovered via a wrapper process chawla et al 2008 then an iterative process is carried out composed of several steps first a minority class instance is selected at random from the training set next its k nearest neighbors 5 by default are obtained finally n of these k instances are randomly chosen to compute the new instances by 866 smote for learning from imbalanced data 15 year anniversary xi1 xi2 r1 r2 xi r3 xi3 r4 xi4 figure 1 an illustration of how to create the synthetic data points in the smote algorithm interpolation to do so the difference between the feature vector sample under consideration and each of the selected neighbors is taken this difference is multiplied by a random number drawn between 0 and 1 and then it is added to the previous feature vector this causes the selection of a random point along the line segment between the features in case of nominal attributes one of the two values is selected at random the whole process is summarized in algorithm 1 algorithm 1 smote algorithm 1 function smote t n k input t n k minority class examples amount of oversampling nearest neighbors output n 100 t synthetic minority class samples variables sample array for original minority class samples newindex keeps a count of number of synthetic successful use of the smote preprocessing algorithm both of which are based on the area bioinformatics specifically we stress a multi class problem of molecular functions 867 ferna ndez garc a herrera imbalanced binary subsets so that new synthetic instances were needed prior to the learning stage of a modular neural network to avoid the bias towards the majority classes 3 extensions to smote in the following we present the most significant smote based approaches proposed in the last 15 years and a set of common properties shared by them we consider smote as a foundation for over sampling with artificial generation of minority class instances for this reason we understand that any preprocessing method in the area of imbalanced classification that is based on the synthetic creation of examples by any type of interpolation or other process has some degree of relationship with the original smote algorithm first in section 3 1 the essential characteristics will be outlined next in section 3 2 we will enumerate all the extensions based on smote proposed in the scientific literature until 868 smote for learning from imbalanced data 15 year anniversary now then each method will be categorized according to the studied properties to provide a comprehensive taxonomy next in section 3 3 we will present a list of smote based multiclassifiers proposed together with their categorization finally section 3 4 will outline the most influential experimental studies presented in the literature involving smote as key point 3 1 properties for categorizing the smote based extensions this section provides a framework for the organization of the smote based extensions that will be presented in sections 3 2 and 3 3 the aspects discussed here consist of 1 initial selection of instances to be oversampled 2 integration with undersampling as step in the technique 3 type of interpolation 4 operation with dimensionality changes 5 adaptive generation of synthetic examples 6 possibility of relabeling and 7 filtering of noisy generated instances these mentioned facets are involved in the definition of the categorization because they determine the way of operation of each technique next we describe in detail each property initial selection of instances to be oversampled it is usual to determine the best candidates to be oversampled in the data before the process of synthetic example generation starts this strategy is intended to reduce the overlapping and noise in the final dataset many techniques opt to choose the instances near to the boundary classes han et al 2005 or to not generate a synthetic example depending on the number of minority class examples belonging to the neighborhood bunkhumpornpat sinapiromsaran lursinsap 2009 although many alternatives of initial selection have been proposed in the literature almost all follow any of the two mentioned strategies two exceptions are the generation of synthetic examples after a lvq optimization process nakamura kajiwara otsuka kimura 2013 and the selection of initial points from the support vectors obtained by a svm cervantes garc a lamont rodr guez mazahua chau ruiz castilla trueba 2017 integration with undersampling the examples belonging to the majority class are also removed by either using a random or an informed technique of undersampling the undersampling step can be either done at the beginning of the oversampling or as an internal operation together with the generation of synthetic examples generally oversampling follows undersampling type of interpolation this property offers varied mechanisms about generation of artificial or synthetic examples and is frequently associated with the main originality of the novel development it defines the way new artificial examples are created and many alternatives can be found the interpolation mechanisms can be range restricted han et al 2005 bunkhumpornpat et al 2009 maciejewski stefanowski 2011 for example by looking not only for nearest neighbours from the minority class but also from majority class creating new examples closer to the selected instance than its neighbor or by using feature weighting hukerikar tumma nikam attar 2011 multiple interpolations de la calleja fuentes 2007 gazzah amara 2008 involving more than two examples or following topologies based on geometric shapes such as ellipses abdi hashemi 2016 and voronoi diagrams young nykl weckman 869 ferna ndez garc a herrera chawla chelberg 2015 and graphs bunkhumpornpat et al 2012 clustering based interpolation barua islam murase 2011 in which the new examples can be either the centroids of the cluster or can be created involving examples that belong to the same cluster interpolations that use different random distributions such as the gaussian sandhan choi 2014 estimations of the probability distribution function of the data gao hong chen harris khalaf 2014b probability smoothing wang li chao cao 2012 preservation of covariances cateni colla vannucci 2011 among data and more complex interpolations such as markov chains das krishnan cook 2015 or q unions rong gong ng 2014 it is even possible to have no interpolation such as when the new data is generated using only a single point through jittering mease wyner buja 2007 gaussians disturbances de la calleja fuentes gonza lez 2008 just simple copies with changes of label stefanowski wilk 2008 or even by combining oversampling with pushing the majority samples out of a sphere koziarski krawczyk wozniak 2017 operation with dimensionality changes this occurs when the technique incorporates either a reduction or augmentation of dimensionality before or during the generation of artificial or synthetic examples the most common approach is to change the dimensionality of the data at the beginning and then to work in the new dimensional space either by reducing it through principal component analysis pca abdi hashemi 2016 or related techniques gu cai zhu 2009 xie jiang ye li 2015 feature selection koto 2014 bagging wang yun li huang ao liu 2013a manifold techniques bellinger drummond japkowicz 2016 and auto encoders bellinger japkowicz drummond 2015 and by using kernel functions mathew luo pang chan 2015 tang he 2015 pe rez ortiz gutie rrez tin o herva s mart nez 2016 also an estimation of the principal components of the data may be used to lead the interpolation tang chen 2008 adaptive generation of synthetic examples the hypothesis of adaptive generation adasyn he bai garcia li 2008 was to use a weighted distribution depending on each minority class example according to their degree of difficulty when learning this way more synthetic data will be generated for some minority class instances that are more complicated to learn compared to other inspired by adasyn lots of techniques incorporate similar mechanisms to control the quantity of new artificial examples to be generated associated with each minority example or subgroups of minority examples alejo garc a pacheco sa nchez 2015 rivera 2017 relabeling the technique offers the choice to relabel the examples belonging to the majority class during the synthetic generation of examples dang tran hirose satou 2015 or replacing the interpolation mechanism blaszczynski deckert stefanowski wilk 2012 filtering of noisy generated instances the first extensions of smote motivated by its well known drawback of generating overlapped and noisy examples was the addition of a noise filtering step just after smote process ends two typical techniques are smote tomeklinks and smote enn batista et al 2004 filtering of artificial examples is a frequent operation that supports the success of smote on real data 870 smote for learning from imbalanced data 15 year anniversary many kind of filters have been proposed for enhancing smote such as greedy filtering strategies puntumapon waiyamai 2012 rough sets based filtering ramentol caballero bello herrera 2012 hu li 2013 ramentol gondres lajes bello caballero cornelis herrera 2016 ensembles based filtering sa ez luengo stefanowski herrera 2015 and bioinspired optimization procedures lo pez triguero carmona garc a herrera 2014 zieba tomczak gonczarek 2015 jiang lu xia 2016 cervantes et al 2017 3 2 smote based extensions for oversampling till date more than 85 extensions of smote have been proposed in the specialized literature this section is devoted to enumerate and categorize them according to the properties studied before table 1 presents an enumeration of the methods reviewed in this paper in this field it is usual that the authors provide a name for their proposal with a few exceptions as we can see in table 1 the most frequent properties exploited by the techniques are the initial selection and adaptive generation of synthetic examples filtering is becoming more common in recent years as well as the use of kernel functions regarding the interpolation procedure it is also usual to replace the original method with other more complex ones such as clustering based or derived from a probabilistic function it is worth mentioning that there is no technique that applies the four mechanisms pertinent to the calibration of the generation of artificial examples selection and removal of harmful examples either synthetic or belonging to the majority class namely initial selection integration with undersampling adaptive generation and filtering all together due to space limitations it is not possible to describe all the reviewed techniques nevertheless we will provide brief explanations for the most well known techniques from table 1 borderline smote han et al 2005 this algorithm draws from the premise of that the examples far from the borderline may contribute little to the classification success thus the technique indentifies those examples which belong to the borderline by using the ratio between the majority and minority examples within the neighborhood of each instance to be oversampled noisy examples those that have all the neighbours from the majority class are not considered the so called dangerous examples with a suitable ratio are oversampled ahc cohen et al 2006 it was the first attempt to use clustering to generate new synthetic examples to balance the data the k means algorithm was used to undersample the majority examples and agglomerative hierarchical clustering was used to oversample the minority examples here the clusters are gathered from all levels of the resulting dendograms and their centroids are interpolated with the original minority class examples adasyn he et al 2008 its main idea proceeds from the assumption of utilizing a weighted distribution depending on the type of minority examples according to their complexity for learning the each minority example safe level smote bunkhumpornpat et al 2009 it assigns each minority example a safe level before generating synthetic instances each synthetic instance will be positiones closer to the largest safe level thus generating all synthetic instances only in safe regions the safe level is the ratio between the number of minority examples within the neighborhood and the safe level ratio depends on the safe level of each instance and that of the examples in its neighborhood the interpolation is controlled by a gap which depends on the safe level ratio of each minority instance dbsmote bunkhumpornpat et al 2012 this algorithm relies on a density based approach of clustering called dbscan and performs oversampling by generating synthetic samples along a shortest path from each minority instance to a pseudocentroid of a minority class cluster dbsmote was inspired by borderline smote in the sense it operates in an overlapping region but unlike borderline smote it also tries to maintain both the minority and majority class accuracies rose menardi torelli 2014 rose is an oversampling technique proposed within a complete framework to obtain classification rules in imbalanced data it is established from the generation of new artificial data from the classes according to a smoothed bootstrap form and the idea behind it is supported by the theoretical wellknown properties of the kernel methods the algorithm samples a new instance using the probability distribution centered at a randomly selected example and depending on a smoothing matrix of scale parameters mwmote barua et al 2014 based on the assumption of that existing oversampling methods may generate wrong synthetic minority samples mwmote analyzes the most difficult minority examples and assigns each them a weight according to their distance from the nearest majority examples the synthetic examples are then generated from the weighted informative minority class instance using a clustering approach ensuring that they must lie inside a minority class cluster mdo abdi hashemi 2016 it is one of the recent multi class approaches inspired by mahalanobis distance mdo builds synthetic examples having the same mahalanobis distance from each examined class mean as the other minority examples thus the region of minority instances can be better learned by preserving the covariance during the generation of synthetic examples along the probability contours also the risk of overlapping between different class regions is reduced 3 3 smote based extensions for ensembles ensembles of et al 2013 and specifically focused on smote to ask about how to discover the proper amount and type of sampling chawla et al 2008 in the work of batista et al 2004 some common resampling approaches are compared and the hybridizations of smote with undersampling was shown to outperform the rest of resampling techniques later prati batista and silva 2015 designed a renewed experimental setup to answer some open ended questions on the relationship and performance between learning paradigms imbalance degrees and proposed solutions more complex analytic studies can be found to analyze data
